messages.subject: CFA comparing 36 groups
parts:
> My name is Elsa, I’m making a Confirmatory Factor Analysis comparing

> 36 groups. The model is composed by three factors and the items are

> dichotomous (0,1).

> I’ve been following the sintax of http://lavaan.ugent.be/?q=node/16,

> however the program doesn’t read the database. Shall you give some

> ideas to solve this problem? 

 You need to specify the name of the data.frame in the cfa() function:

 fit<-cfa (mymodel, data=mydata, group="gr", group.equal=c("loadings","thresholds"), ordered= c("E_10", "E_40","N_23","N_31","P_30","P_65"), estimator='DWLS')

 Note I added the second argument: data=mydata

 Hope this helps,

 Yves Rosseel.

Thank very much for the help.

 However, I have a new problem:   

 system is computationally singular: reciprocal condition number = 1.16278e-50

Could it be happening that there are too many groups? 

Thank you

There is no way of telling what caused this without having the data
itself. I you can send me the data (together with the R script), I am
willing to have a look at it.

In the mean time, I would suggest trying the following (if you haven't
done so yourself):

1) fit the model for all groups (ie omit the 'group' argument)
2) fit the model for each group separately
